title: 5.2 Small Group · Group 2
contentObjective: I can find the area of a triangle using the formula A = ½ × base × height, explain why the method works, and use it on a problem I have not seen before.
languageObjective: I can justify my answer to a skeptic and connect it to a second strategy or representation.

revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Painting a Cabin
revealWordProblem.text: The front of this A-frame cabin is a triangle with a base of 34 ft and a height of 23¾ ft. Find the area of the triangular front that needs to be painted.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: Area = ½ × base × height = ½ × 34 × 23¾. First, 23¾ = 23.75, so 34 × 23.75 = 807.5. Then take half: 807.5 ÷ 2 = 403.75. The triangular front of the cabin has an area of 403.75 square feet.

vocabulary.definition: The space inside a triangle. A triangle is half of a rectangle with the same base and height, so A = ½ × b × h.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El espacio dentro de un triángulo. Un triángulo es la mitad de un rectángulo con la misma base y altura, por eso A = ½ × b × h.
vocabulary.visual: A = ½ × b × h; if b = 8 and h = 5, then A = ½ × 8 × 5 = 20 square units
vocabulary.cloze: The space inside a triangle, found with A = ½ × b × h, is the ___.

vocabulary.definition: Any side of a triangle can be the base. Once you pick a base, the height must be measured perpendicular (at a 90° angle) to it.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Cualquier lado de un triángulo puede ser la base. Una vez que eliges la base, la altura debe medirse perpendicular (en un ángulo de 90°) a ella.
vocabulary.visual: Any side can be the base: choose the 10 cm side and b = 10 cm, then draw the height from the opposite vertex at 90° to that side in A = ½ × b × h
vocabulary.cloze: The side of a triangle you measure the height from at a 90° angle is the ___.

vocabulary.definition: The straight-up distance from the base to the top corner.
vocabulary.definitionEs: La distancia recta desde la base hasta la esquina de arriba.
vocabulary.visual: A dashed vertical line from the top point straight down to the base at a 90° angle — like dropping a plumb line
vocabulary.cloze: The perpendicular distance from the base to the opposite vertex is the ___.

vocabulary.definition: How much space is inside a flat shape.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Cuánto espacio hay dentro de una figura plana.
vocabulary.visual: A triangle with b = 8 and h = 6 has area = ½ × 8 × 6 = 24 sq units — exactly half the rectangle around it
vocabulary.cloze: The amount of flat space inside a triangle is its ___.

vocabulary.definition: Two lines that meet to make a square corner (90 degrees).
vocabulary.definitionEs: Dos líneas que se unen formando una esquina recta (90 grados).
vocabulary.visual: The corner of a book or a door frame — the edges meet at exactly 90°, shown by a small square symbol
vocabulary.cloze: Two lines that meet at a 90° angle are ___.

examples.text: Two lines meeting at a 90° angle
examples.why: Perpendicular lines form a right angle.
Those are parallel lines, not perpendicular.

vocabulary.definition: A shape made by putting two or more simple shapes together.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una figura formada al juntar dos o más figuras simples.
vocabulary.visual: A house shape = a rectangle (the walls) + a triangle (the roof); total area = rectangle area + triangle area
vocabulary.cloze: A shape made of two or more basic shapes combined is a ___.

vocabulary.definition: A math rule written with symbols.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una regla matemática escrita con símbolos.
vocabulary.visual: A = ½ × b × h means Area equals one-half times base times height; for b = 12 and h = 8, A = 48
vocabulary.cloze: A math rule written with symbols, like A = ½ × b × h, is a ___.

vocabulary.definition: Two lines or sides that stay the same distance apart and never meet.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Dos líneas o lados que se mantienen a la misma distancia y nunca se cruzan.
vocabulary.visual: The top and bottom of a parallelogram never get closer together — matching arrowheads (›) mark one parallel pair, double arrowheads (››) mark the other.
vocabulary.cloze: Two sides that stay the same distance apart and never meet are ___.

conceptIntro.heading: Push further — How do we find the area of a triangle?
conceptIntro.intro: You already can do this. So we go up a level, not up a number: find what is always true, show it a second way, and be ready to defend it with a reason instead of an answer.
conceptIntro.keyIdea: Area of a triangle = ½ × base × height. A triangle is exactly half of a rectangle with the same base and height — and you can say why it is true, and where it would stop being true.

I put in the numbers: A = ½ × 12 × 8.
I take half: ½ × 96 = 48. So the area is 48 square feet.

onLevel.title: Spot the Common Mistake

workedExample.label: Identify base and height
workedExample.labelEs: Identifica la base y la altura

onLevel.correctWork: There is only ONE ½ in the formula, not two. The student halved both the base and the height. Multiply base × height first, then take half just once: 12 × 7 = 84, then ½ × 84 = 42 sq ft.
hints: How many times does the ½ appear in A = ½ × base × height — once or twice?
Multiply 12 × 7 = 84 first, then take half a single time: ½ × 84 = 42 sq ft.
onLevel.explanation: There is only ONE ½ in A = ½ × base × height, but the calculation halved the base and the height separately. Multiply first, then halve a single time: 12 × 7 = 84, and ½ × 84 = 42 sq ft. Halving twice cuts the area to a quarter of the rectangle, which is why 21 came out as exactly half of the true answer.
onLevel.explanationEs: En A = ½ × base × altura hay solo UN ½, pero el cálculo tomó la mitad de la base y la mitad de la altura por separado. Multiplica primero y toma la mitad una sola vez: 12 × 7 = 84, y ½ × 84 = 42 sq ft. Tomar la mitad dos veces reduce el área a la cuarta parte del rectángulo, y por eso 21 resultó ser exactamente la mitad de la respuesta correcta.
onLevel.correctWorkEs: Solo hay UN ½ en la fórmula, no dos. El estudiante partió a la mitad tanto la base como la altura. Multiplica base × altura primero, y luego toma la mitad una sola vez: 12 × 7 = 84, luego ½ × 84 = 42 pies cuadrados.

onLevel.title: Find the Area Error

workedExample.label: Identify base and height
workedExample.labelEs: Identifica la base y la altura

onLevel.correctWork: 14 × 9 = 126, then ½ × 126 = 63 sq m. The student added 14 + 9 = 23 instead of multiplying 14 × 9 = 126.
hints: Look at Step 4. What operation should happen between 14 and 9?
14 × 9 ≠ 23. The student added instead of multiplied.
onLevel.explanation: The setup A = ½ × 14 × 9 is written correctly, but the calculation added 14 + 9 = 23 instead of multiplying. Base and height must be multiplied: 14 × 9 = 126, and then ½ × 126 = 63 sq m.
onLevel.explanationEs: El planteamiento A = ½ × 14 × 9 está bien escrito, pero el cálculo sumó 14 + 9 = 23 en vez de multiplicar. La base y la altura se multiplican: 14 × 9 = 126, y luego ½ × 126 = 63 sq m.
onLevel.correctWorkEs: 14 × 9 = 126, luego ½ × 126 = 63 m cuadrados. El estudiante sumó 14 + 9 = 23 en lugar de multiplicar 14 × 9 = 126.

onLevel.prompt: A rectangle is 12 ft by 8 ft. A diagonal line cuts it into two triangles. What is the area of each triangle? Explain how the triangle area formula relates to the rectangle area formula.
onLevel.sentenceFrame: The rectangle's area is ___ because ___. Each triangle's area is ___ because a diagonal splits a rectangle into ___ equal triangles, so A = ½ × ___ × ___ = ___.
onLevel.hint: Write the formula with given numbers; solve step by step.
hints: Start with the rectangle: its area comes from 12 × 8. The diagonal splits that area into two identical pieces.
Each triangle keeps the same base (12) and height (8) as the rectangle — so its area is half the rectangle's.
Compute 12 × 8, halve it for one triangle, then check with ½ × 12 × 8. Explain why both paths give the same number.
onLevel.explanation: The rectangle's area is 12 × 8 = 96 sq ft, and one diagonal cuts it into two identical triangles, so each triangle is 96 ÷ 2 = 48 sq ft. The formula says the same thing: each triangle keeps the rectangle's base of 12 and height of 8, and A = ½ × 12 × 8 = 48 sq ft. The ½ in the triangle formula IS that diagonal cut.
onLevel.explanationEs: El área del rectángulo es 12 × 8 = 96 sq ft, y una diagonal lo corta en dos triángulos idénticos, así que cada triángulo mide 96 ÷ 2 = 48 sq ft. La fórmula dice lo mismo: cada triángulo conserva la base de 12 y la altura de 8 del rectángulo, y A = ½ × 12 × 8 = 48 sq ft. El ½ de la fórmula del triángulo ES ese corte diagonal.
onLevel.promptEs: Un rectángulo mide 12 pies por 8 pies. Una línea diagonal lo corta en dos triángulos. ¿Cuál es el área de cada triángulo? Explica cómo se relaciona la fórmula del área del triángulo con la del rectángulo.
hintsEs: Empieza con el rectángulo: su área sale de 12 × 8. La diagonal parte esa área en dos piezas idénticas.
Cada triángulo conserva la misma base (12) y altura (8) del rectángulo, así que su área es la mitad de la del rectángulo.
Calcula 12 × 8, sácale la mitad para un triángulo y luego comprueba con ½ × 12 × 8. Explica por qué ambos caminos dan el mismo número.

onLevel.stem: A triangular window in the firm's lobby has a base of 10 ft and a height of 6 ft. What is its area?
onLevel.explanation: A = ½ × base × height = ½ × 10 × 6 = ½ × 60 = 30 sq ft. The triangle is half of the 10 × 6 = 60 rectangle it fits inside.
choiceFeedback: One pair of parallel sides = trapezoid.
Does this have one or two pairs?
Not quite. A = ½ × base × height = ½ × 10 × 6 = ½ × 60 = ___ sq ft.
onLevel.stemEs: Una ventana triangular en el vestíbulo de la firma tiene una base de 10 ft y una altura de 6 ft. ¿Cuál es su área?
onLevel.explanationEs: A = ½ × base × altura = ½ × 10 × 6 = ½ × 60 = 30 sq ft. El triángulo es la mitad del rectángulo de 10 × 6 = 60 en el que cabe.
hints: A triangle covers exactly half of the rectangle that has the same base and the same height.
Use A = ½ × base × height: multiply the two measurements first, then take half of that product.
Start with 10 × 6 = 60 sq ft for the whole rectangle, then take half of 60 to finish.
hintsEs: Un triángulo cubre exactamente la mitad del rectángulo que tiene la misma base y la misma altura.
Usa A = ½ × base × altura: multiplica primero las dos medidas y luego toma la mitad de ese producto.
Empieza con 10 × 6 = 60 sq ft para el rectángulo completo y después toma la mitad de 60 para terminar.

extending.stem: A triangular roof panel on the blueprint has a base of 7 ft and a height of 4 ft. What is its area?
extending.explanation: A = ½ × base × height = ½ × 7 × 4 = ½ × 28 = 14 sq ft. Multiply base × height first (28), then take half (14).
choiceFeedback: A trapezoid has TWO parallel bases.
Add both bases in the formula.
The height is perpendicular between the bases.
extending.stemEs: Un panel triangular del techo en el plano tiene una base de 7 ft y una altura de 4 ft. ¿Cuál es su área?
extending.explanationEs: A = ½ × base × altura = ½ × 7 × 4 = ½ × 28 = 14 sq ft. Multiplica primero base × altura (28) y después toma la mitad (14).
hints: The area of a triangle is A = ½ × base × height, and the ½ is there because a triangle is half of a rectangle.
Multiply the base by the height first, then cut that result in half.
Multiply 7 × 4 to find the surrounding rectangle's area, then take half of that product for the triangle.
hintsEs: El área de un triángulo es A = ½ × base × altura, y el ½ está ahí porque un triángulo es la mitad de un rectángulo.
Multiplica primero la base por la altura y después divide ese resultado a la mitad.
Multiplica 7 × 4 para hallar el área del rectángulo que lo rodea y luego toma la mitad de ese producto para el triángulo.

extending.stem: On the blueprint, a triangular garden bed has a base of 11 ft and a height of 6 ft. What is its area?
extending.explanation: A = ½ × base × height = ½ × 11 × 6 = ½ × 66 = 33 sq ft.
choiceFeedback: That's base × height — a triangle is half of that.
You added base and height — use ½ × base × height instead.
Recompute ½ × 11 × 6 carefully.
extending.stemEs: En el plano, un jardín triangular tiene una base de 11 ft y una altura de 6 ft. ¿Cuál es su área?
extending.explanationEs: A = ½ × base × altura = ½ × 11 × 6 = ½ × 66 = 33 sq ft.
hints: Every triangle's area comes from A = ½ × base × height.
With an odd base, it is easier to multiply base × height first and take half at the end.
Start with 11 × 6 for the rectangle that surrounds the triangle, then take half of that result.
hintsEs: El área de todo triángulo se obtiene con A = ½ × base × altura.
Con una base impar, es más fácil multiplicar primero base × altura y tomar la mitad al final.
Empieza con 11 × 6 para el rectángulo que rodea al triángulo y después toma la mitad de ese resultado.

extending.title: Level 2 Extension — Find the Half-Area Mistake

workedExample.label: Identify base and height
workedExample.labelEs: Identifica la base y la altura

extending.correctWork: The intern stopped at base × height = 16 × 9 = 144, but that is the area of the whole rectangle. A triangle is only half of that rectangle, so you must still take half: ½ × 144 = 72 sq ft.
hints: A triangle fits inside a matching rectangle. Is 144 the rectangle or the triangle?
The formula has a ½ in it. The intern multiplied 16 × 9 but never took half — finish by computing ½ × 144.
extending.titleEs: Extensión de Nivel 2: encuentra el error de la mitad del área
extending.explanation: Multiplying 16 × 9 = 144 is only half the job — that product is the area of the rectangle that surrounds the triangle. The formula still has a ½ waiting to be used, so the triangular wall is ½ × 144 = 72 sq ft.
extending.explanationEs: Multiplicar 16 × 9 = 144 es solo la mitad del trabajo: ese producto es el área del rectángulo que rodea al triángulo. La fórmula todavía tiene un ½ esperando, así que el muro triangular mide ½ × 144 = 72 sq ft.
extending.correctWorkEs: El practicante se detuvo en base × altura = 16 × 9 = 144, pero esa es el área del rectángulo completo. Un triángulo es solo la mitad de ese rectángulo, así que todavía falta tomar la mitad: ½ × 144 = 72 pies cuadrados.

extending.stem: What is the area of a triangle with base 10 cm and height 6 cm?
extending.explanation: A = ½ × b × h = ½ × 10 × 6 = 30 square centimeters.
choiceFeedback: 60 is base × height — the full rectangle. A triangle is half of that, so multiply by ½.
16 comes from adding 10 + 6. Area means multiply the base and height, then take half.
The number is right, but cm measures length. Area needs square units (sq cm).
hints: You have a base of 10 cm and a height of 6 cm — a triangle needs only those two, plus one special step.
A triangle is half of a rectangle: use A = ½ × b × h. If you only multiply, your answer is twice too big.
Multiply 10 × 6, then take half of the product. Area units are square centimeters.
extending.stemEs: ¿Cuál es el área de un triángulo con base de 10 cm y altura de 6 cm?
extending.explanationEs: A = ½ × b × h = ½ × 10 × 6 = 30 centímetros cuadrados.
hintsEs: Tienes una base de 10 cm y una altura de 6 cm: un triángulo solo necesita esas dos, más un paso especial.
Un triángulo es la mitad de un rectángulo: usa A = ½ × b × h. Si solo multiplicas, tu respuesta sale al doble.
Multiplica 10 × 6 y luego saca la mitad del producto. Las unidades de área son centímetros cuadrados.

extending.stem: A triangle has an area of 24 sq ft and a base of 8 ft. What is the height?
choiceFeedback: 3 is 24 ÷ 8 — but that skips the ½. Double the area first: 2 × 24 = 48, then divide by the base.
16 comes from 24 − 8. Use h = (2 × area) ÷ base instead of subtracting.
12 is half of 24 — that divides by 2 instead of doubling. Try 2 × 24 = 48, then ÷ 8.
hints: The area (24 sq ft) and base (8 ft) are given — you're solving backwards for the height.
Simplify first: ½ × 8 = 4, so the equation becomes 24 = 4 × h.
Divide 24 by 4 to find the height in feet.
extending.stemEs: Un triángulo tiene un área de 24 sq ft y una base de 8 ft. ¿Cuál es la altura?
hintsEs: Te dan el área (24 pies²) y la base (8 pies): estás despejando la altura al revés.
Simplifica primero: ½ × 8 = 4, así que la ecuación se vuelve 24 = 4 × h.
Divide 24 entre 4 para hallar la altura en pies.

extending.stem: Why do we divide by 2 when finding the area of a triangle?
choices: A triangle is exactly half of a rectangle with the same base and height
The base is always twice the height
We always divide area formulas by 2
extending.explanation: A triangle with base b and height h fits inside a rectangle with the same base and height. The triangle covers exactly half the rectangle, so A = ½ × b × h.
choiceFeedback: Which two sides are parallel?
The height is perpendicular to them.
Identify bases and height correctly.
hints: Think about drawing a diagonal across a rectangle — what two shapes does it create?
Compare a triangle to a rectangle with the same base and height. How much of the rectangle does the triangle cover?
Sketch a rectangle, draw one diagonal, and shade one triangle. What fraction of the rectangle did you shade?
extending.stemEs: ¿Por qué dividimos entre 2 al hallar el área de un triángulo?
extending.explanationEs: Un triángulo con base b y altura h cabe dentro de un rectángulo con la misma base y la misma altura. El triángulo cubre exactamente la mitad del rectángulo, así que A = ½ × b × h.
choicesEs: Un triángulo es exactamente la mitad de un rectángulo con la misma base y la misma altura
La base siempre es el doble de la altura
Siempre dividimos entre 2 las fórmulas de área
hintsEs: Piensa en trazar una diagonal en un rectángulo: ¿qué dos figuras se forman?
Compara un triángulo con un rectángulo de la misma base y altura. ¿Qué parte del rectángulo cubre el triángulo?
Dibuja un rectángulo, traza una diagonal y sombrea un triángulo. ¿Qué fracción del rectángulo sombreaste?

extending.stem: What is the area of a triangle with base 14 ft and height 6 ft?
choiceFeedback: Exactly ONE pair of parallel sides is a trapezoid.
TWO pairs would be a parallelogram.
Count the parallel pairs.
hints: Base 14 ft and height 6 ft — remember what makes a triangle's area different from a rectangle's.
Use A = ½ × b × h: compute the full product first, then halve it. Area needs square units.
Find 14 × 6, then take half of that product. Write the units as sq ft.
extending.stemEs: ¿Cuál es el área de un triángulo con base de 14 ft y altura de 6 ft?
hintsEs: Base de 14 pies y altura de 6 pies: recuerda qué hace distinta el área de un triángulo de la de un rectángulo.
Usa A = ½ × b × h: calcula primero el producto completo y luego sácale la mitad. El área necesita unidades cuadradas.
Halla 14 × 6 y luego saca la mitad de ese producto. Escribe las unidades como pies².

extending.hint: Use A = ½ × b × h; work backwards for missing values.
hints: Gardens A and D are missing area; Gardens B and C are missing a base or height — those need backwards steps.
Missing area: ½ × b × h. Missing base or height: double the area first, then divide by the measurement you know.
Garden B: double 27 to get 54, then divide 54 by the base 9 to find the height.
extending.explanation: Two rows run forward and two run backward. Garden A: ½ × 12 × 8 = 48 sq ft, and Garden D: ½ × 15 × 4 = 30 sq ft. When the base or height is missing, double the area first: Garden B, 27 × 2 = 54, then 54 ÷ 9 = 6 ft of height; Garden C, 35 × 2 = 70, then 70 ÷ 10 = 7 ft of base.
extending.explanationEs: Dos filas van hacia adelante y dos van hacia atrás. Garden A: ½ × 12 × 8 = 48 sq ft, y Garden D: ½ × 15 × 4 = 30 sq ft. Cuando falta la base o la altura, primero duplica el área: Garden B, 27 × 2 = 54, y luego 54 ÷ 9 = 6 ft de altura; Garden C, 35 × 2 = 70, y luego 70 ÷ 10 = 7 ft de base.
hintsEs: A los Jardines A y D les falta el área; a los Jardines B y C les falta una base o una altura, y esos necesitan pasos al revés.
Falta el área: ½ × b × h. Falta la base o la altura: duplica primero el área y luego divide entre la medida que conoces.
Jardín B: duplica 27 para obtener 54 y luego divide 54 entre la base 9 para hallar la altura.

practice.commonMistake: A common mistake in Area of Triangles is forgetting the ½ — students multiply base × height like a rectangle and stop there, or they use the triangle's slanted side instead of the perpendicular height that's already given. Always check: did I take half, and did I use the straight-up height, not the slanted side?

connect.scenario: A homeowner wants to paint one triangular wall of an A-frame cabin. The wall has a base of 20 feet and a height of 14 feet. One can of paint covers 50 square feet.
connect.promptQuestion: How many cans of paint does the homeowner need?
connect.prompt: The wall's area is ___ sq ft because A = 1/2 × ___ × ___. She needs ___ cans because ___ ÷ 50 = ___.

check.stem: What is the area of the triangular wall?
check.explanation: A = ½ × base × height = ½ × 20 × 14 = 140 sq ft.

check.stem: How many cans of paint does she need?
check.explanation: 140 ÷ 50 = 2.8. You cannot buy 0.8 of a can, so round UP to 3 cans.

check.stem: Why round up instead of down?
choices: Because 2 cans cover only 100 sq ft, which is not enough for 140
Because paint is always sold in threes
Because 2.8 rounds to 3 by the usual rule
Because the wall might be bigger
check.explanation: Two cans cover 2 × 50 = 100 sq ft, leaving 40 sq ft unpainted. In a 'how many containers' problem you always round up.

connect.modelAnswer: A = ½ × 20 × 14 = 140 sq ft. Since 140 ÷ 50 = 2.8 and you cannot buy part of a can, the homeowner needs 3 cans of paint.
